title: Petrol (Motor Spirit) Consumption (Monthly, PPAC)
description: Monthly domestic consumption of Petrol (Motor Spirit) in India, in thousand tonnes, from PPAC (Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas), compiled from oil-company sales plus private direct imports. Petrol demand reflects private vehicle use and two-wheeler fleets and includes ethanol blended into petrol. The latest month is provisional and is usually published within about a week of the following month.
source: Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell (PPAC), Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

qna.question: What does this measure?
qna.answer: Domestic consumption of Petrol (Motor Spirit) (MS in PPAC tables), in thousand tonnes per month. PPAC defines consumption as the sum of oil-company sales in the domestic market and private direct imports (which are pro-rated until actual data arrive).^Total petroleum consumption is already on the dashboard as Petroleum Consumption; this page gives the product detail.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Use the YoY view to remove seasonality (kerosene, LPG, bitumen and petcoke have strong seasonal patterns). Petrol growth is steady (high single digits) in normal years; a sharp slowdown usually follows price hikes or poor consumer sentiment.^Months in 2020-21 are distorted by COVID lockdowns, so YoY growth for 2021-22 is mainly a base effect.

qna.question: Definitions, revisions and caveats
qna.answer: All figures are provisional and are revised: PPAC replaces each month as better oil-company and customs data arrive (the latest two to three months, especially the private direct import share, can change). The series is built from PPAC's yearly tables (April-March) back to April 2020; older years are only in PPAC's login-protected historical file and are not used.^PPAC groups some products (for example 'Others' and LDO) separately; they are not shown here.
